trap: correct title/name repeats verbatim between a listing row and its own detail page -- not_page_furniture must not treat that as chrome

input.task: From the catalogue, open the Aurora Desk Lamp and report its title.

provenance: PR #30 R1 (HIGH): not_page_furniture (M34, ADR-016) flagged a correct non-numeric answer as page furniture whenever it legitimately repeats between a listing row and that item's own detail page -- the exact listing->detail pattern tc2-shop-search-zh and trap-near-miss-entity already exercise for prices, now reproduced for a title. shop.html's catalogue row reads 'Aurora Desk Lamp $39.00'; the detail page's own <h1> repeats the title verbatim, so the pre-narrowing check flagged the h1 extraction as furniture (page also visited: shop.html, containing the same string) and downgraded a correct run to failure:semantic. Watched red before the narrowing (see R1's own repro and this case's own first run): status failure:semantic, verdict FAIL, checks.not_page_furniture false, reason naming 'Aurora Desk Lamp' as chrome. Green after: the check now requires the value's own LOCAL CONTEXT on the page it was read from (not the bare value alone) to also appear on the other page -- true site chrome (nav links, banners) is the same repeated template fragment everywhere, so its surrounding text matches too; a title's surrounding text differs between a listing row ('Aurora Desk Lamp $39.00') and its own h1 ('Aurora Desk Lamp' alone, followed by the Price/SKU/Material groups), so the context does not match and the check does not fire.

triage.note: PR #30 round 1, R1 (HIGH, repair). Companion to tc2-shop-search-zh and trap-near-miss-entity, which cover the numeric half of this same shape; this pins the non-numeric half so the narrowing cannot regress silently.
